title: "Scrape: recessions"
engine: knitr
---

The "List of recessions in the United States" table has a flat header, so renaming the columns is the only reshaping it needs. The code below fetches the page with `requests`, then `pandas.read_html()` finds every table on it and `match=` picks out the one with "GDP decline" in its header.

```{python}
#| label: scrape-recessions
#| eval: false
import io
import pandas as pd
import requests

url = "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_recessions_in_the_United_States"
html = requests.get(url, headers={"User-Agent": "wikimill-project/0.1"}).text

tables = pd.read_html(io.StringIO(html), match="GDP decline")
recessions = tables[0]
recessions.columns = [
    "name", "period_range", "duration", "time_since_previous",
    "peak_unemployment", "gdp_decline", "characteristics"
]
recessions.to_csv("data/recessions.csv", index=False)
recessions.head()
```

This chunk is shown for reference only (`eval: false`), so rendering the site doesn't hit Wikipedia. Run `python src/scrape_recessions.py` from the project root to refresh `data/recessions.csv`. See [clean_recessions.qmd](clean_recessions.qmd) for the next step.
